title: Scaling, composition 0.95 (else default)
html:
Scaling, composition 0.95 (else default)

Question: With composition 0.95 and everything else as the default graph, how does what each society achieves grow with its budget?

Answer: At budgets 50–100: best OSO (α = 0.2, β = 1). Against traditional, clearly better on hardest level, knowledge found (bits) and knowledge per unit of money; no clear difference on targets solved, bounty value, ROI and waste. At budget 200: best OSO (α = 0.2, β = 1). Against traditional, clearly better on hardest level, targets solved, bounty value, ROI, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money and waste. At budget 400: best OSO (α = 0.8, β = 1). Against traditional, clearly better on hardest level, targets solved, bounty value, ROI, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money and waste. At budget 800: best OSO (α = 0.8, β = 1). Against traditional, clearly better on hardest level, targets solved, bounty value, ROI, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money, money to the main level and waste. At budgets 1600–25600: best OSO (α = 0.8, β = 1). Against traditional, clearly better on ROI, knowledge per unit of money, money to the main level and waste; no clear difference on hardest level, targets solved, bounty value and knowledge found (bits). At budgets 51200–102400: best OSO (α = 0.8, β = 1). Against traditional, clearly better on ROI, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money, money to the main level and waste; no clear difference on hardest level, targets solved and bounty value. (Compared at each budget; 8 measures, a clear difference is more than 2.7 standard errors.)

  • Budget 50: hardest level: 2.60 against traditional 0.00, clearly better. targets solved: 0.05 against traditional 0.00, no clear difference.
  • Budget 100: hardest level: 4.55 against traditional 0.00, clearly better. targets solved: 0.25 against traditional 0.00, no clear difference.
  • Budget 200: hardest level: 5.85 against traditional 0.00, clearly better. targets solved: 1.30 against traditional 0.00, clearly better.

Design (fixed before the run): compared four societies × budgets 50 to 102400 · held the same: a generated idea graph (6 levels × 8 ideas, 2 parents each, sequences of 3 bits growing by 2 per level, composition 0.95), 12 identical agents, budget 50 split equally, no mint, no validation · measure: all of hardest level, targets solved, bounty value, ROI, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money, money to the main level, waste · 20 runs per row.

Caveats:

  • A simulation with guessed parameters: it shows how the rules play out, not that they work.
Details

The simple model on a generated idea graph (6 levels × 8 ideas, 2 parents each, sequences of 3 bits growing by 2 per level, composition 0.95); each run draws its own graph. Only α and β vary. Held fixed: 12 identical agents, a budget of 50 split equally every round (ρ = 0), no mint, no validation.

Values are mean ± standard deviation over runs.
